# Polyshares

> Polyshares is a private investment firm with two mandates. It represents companies
> licensing their operational data to the buyers paying for it, and it acquires lower
> middle market businesses outright. Data licensing deals typically pay the company
> $100K to $1M, are non-dilutive, and carry a fee taken from the proceeds.

Polyshares works for the seller. It prices the asset, holds the buyer relationships,
handles anonymization before anything leaves the company's systems, and negotiates the
license. It is not a marketplace and does not list client data on one. The company keeps
its equity, keeps ownership of the underlying data, and takes no buyer meetings.

Key facts, current as of August 2026:

- Deal size: typically $100,000 to $1,000,000 paid to the company.
- Structure: a license to defined operational data. No equity, no debt, no dilution.
- Eligibility: any company with real operating history, whether venture backed, middle
  market, or founder owned. Depth of record matters more than headcount or revenue.
- Fee: taken from the proceeds. If nothing sells, the company owes nothing.
- Timeline: terms papered within a week of the first conversation; funds in the company
  account in eight to twelve weeks, on the buyer closing.
- Anonymization: handled by Polyshares, before any material leaves the company.
- Second mandate: outright acquisition of lower middle market businesses, currently
  focused on MSPs and IT providers.

"Operational data" means the working record a business produces by running: Slack and
Teams threads, Drive and SharePoint, email, CRM history, support tickets, design files,
call recordings, and accounting or ERP exports. What buyers pay for is the visible
reasoning inside that record rather than its raw volume.

## Core pages

- [Data licensing](https://polyshares.com/data-licensing): The mandate in full. Terms, who qualifies, what buyers pay for, and what Polyshares is not.
- [Check your data](https://polyshares.com/intake): Five-question intake that returns whether there is a market for a given company's record.
- [The firm](https://polyshares.com/team): The four partners, their operating histories, and their roles on a mandate.
- [Track record](https://polyshares.com/case-studies): Companies the partners founded, bought, scaled, and sold.

## Answers

- [How to sell your company's data to AI companies](https://polyshares.com/sell-company-data-to-ai): The five steps, starting with proving the company owns the records.
- [What your company's data is worth](https://polyshares.com/what-is-my-company-data-worth): Why depth beats volume, what raises the price, and what caps it.
- [Who buys company data](https://polyshares.com/who-buys-company-data): Frontier labs, applied AI companies, and aggregators, and what each checks first.
- [Licensing versus selling outright](https://polyshares.com/data-licensing-vs-selling-data): Why a license usually pays more over the life of a growing record.
- [Whether you can legally license your company's data](https://polyshares.com/is-it-legal-to-sell-company-data): Ownership, customer agreements, and personal information. Not legal advice.
- [How a data licensing deal works](https://polyshares.com/how-data-licensing-deals-work): The sequence from first call to funds received.
